scenario: Update store profile with all valid data
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Change Store Name, Description and Contact Number to the test data.
2. Upload the logo and the banner.
3. Click Save.
4. Refresh the Store Settings page.
5. Log in as Buyer 1 in another browser and open Seller 1's store page.
6. Search for 'Maria Clara Handicrafts PH' as Buyer 1.
data:
Store Name: Maria Clara Handicrafts PH
Description: Handwoven bags and home decor from Bulacan artisans.
Contact Number: 09189876543
Logo: store_logo.png (300 KB)
Banner: store_banner.jpg (1.8 MB)
expected: A success message is shown. After refresh every field shows the saved value. The buyer's store page shows the new name, description, logo and banner, and the store search finds the new name. The old name no longer appears anywhere on the buyer side. No other store's data changes.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Clear Store Name and click Save.
2. Refresh, clear Contact Number and click Save.
3. Refresh, clear Pickup Address (each part) and click Save.
4. Refresh the page after each attempt.
data: Clear in turn: Store Name, Contact Number, Region, City / Municipality, Barangay, Street Address
expected: Each attempt is blocked. A required-field message appears on the blank field only. After refresh, the original values are still saved; nothing was changed.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Enter only spaces in Store Name.
2. Click Save.
expected: Saving is blocked with the required-field message (spaces are trimmed, so the field counts as empty). The old store name is kept.

scenario: Store name already used by another store
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Enter each store name in the test data, one per attempt.
2. Click Save each time.
data:
RV Gadget Hub
rv gadget hub
'  RV Gadget Hub  ' (with leading and trailing spaces)
expected: All three are blocked with a message that the store name is already taken (the check ignores case and leading or trailing spaces). Seller 1's name is unchanged.

scenario: Store name length at the limits
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Enter each store name in the test data, one per attempt.
2. Click Save each time and note the result.
data:
2 characters: MC (reject)
3 characters: MCH (accept)
30 characters: Maria Clara Handicrafts Bulaca (accept)
31 characters: Maria Clara Handicrafts Bulacan (reject)
expected: 2 and 31 characters are rejected with a message stating the 3–30 character limit. 3 and 30 characters are saved exactly as typed. The field does not silently cut off the 31st character.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Paste a 500-character description and save.
2. Paste a 501-character description and save.
expected: 500 characters are saved and shown in full on the store page. 501 characters are rejected with a limit message, or the field stops input at 500; the saved text is never cut silently after saving.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps: 1. Enter each contact number, one per attempt, and save.
data:
09189876543 (accept)
+639189876543 (accept)
0918987654 (10 digits, reject)
091898765432 (12 digits, reject)
0918-ABC-6543 (reject)
08189876543 (does not start with 09, reject)
expected: Only the two valid Philippine mobile formats are accepted. Each invalid value shows a format message and nothing is saved.

scenario: Logo and banner file type and size
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Upload each file as the logo, one at a time, and save.
2. Repeat every file as the banner.
3. Refresh after each attempt.
data:
size_4.9MB.jpg (accept)
size_5.0MB.jpg (accept)
size_5.1MB.jpg (reject)
price_list.docx (reject)
installer.exe (reject)
renamed_exe.jpg (reject)
expected: The 4.9 MB and 5.0 MB images are accepted. The 5.1 MB file, the DOCX, the EXE and the renamed EXE are rejected with a message naming the allowed types and the 5 MB limit. After a rejection the previous logo or banner is still shown.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store is Open. Buyer 1 has P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Turn on vacation mode and save.
2. As Buyer 1, open the store page and P-02.
3. Click Add to Cart and Buy Now.
4. Open the cart, select P-02 and click Check Out.
5. As Buyer 2, search for P-02.
expected: P-02 still appears in search and on the store page with an 'On vacation' label. Add to Cart and Buy Now are disabled. Checkout of the cart item is blocked with a vacation message. No order can be created for any Seller 1 product while vacation mode is on.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Vacation mode is on. Buyer 1 has P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Turn off vacation mode and save.
2. As Buyer 1, refresh P-02.
3. Check out the cart item by COD.
expected: The 'On vacation' label is gone, Add to Cart and Buy Now are enabled, and the order is placed normally.

scenario: Seller that is not Approved tries to publish
pre: Logged in as Seller 3 (Pending Approval).
steps:
1. Add a product with all valid data.
2. Click Publish.
3. Click Save as Draft.
4. As Buyer 1, search for the product name.
data: Product: Handwoven Coin Purse, ₱120.00, stock 10, 0.1 kg, product_front.jpg
expected: Publish is disabled or blocked with a message that the store must be approved first. Save as Draft succeeds and the product shows as Draft. The product does not appear anywhere on the buyer side.

scenario: Script and HTML in text fields
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Settings page is open.
steps:
1. Enter the test data in Description.
2. Save and open the store page as Buyer 1.
3. Open the browser console.
expected: The text is shown literally or with the tags removed. No pop-up appears, no image error triggers a script, and the console shows no script execution.

scenario: Seller cannot edit another store's settings
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Open Store Settings and note the store ID in the URL or request.
2. Change it to Seller 2's store ID and reload or resend the save request.
expected: Access is denied (403, not found, or redirect). No Seller 2 data is shown and nothing about Seller 2's store changes.

scenario: Create a store category and assign a product
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Categories page is open.
steps:
1. Click Add Category, enter the name and save.
2. Edit P-01 and add the new category.
3. As Buyer 1, open Seller 1's store page and click the new category.
expected: The category is listed in Store Categories with 1 product. On the store page it appears and shows P-01 only.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Store Categories page is open.
steps:
1. Try to save a category with each name, one per attempt.
2. Refresh the list after each attempt.
data:
Empty (reject)
'   ' spaces only (reject)
1 character: B (accept)
50 characters (accept)
51 characters (reject)
expected: Empty, spaces-only and 51-character names are blocked with a message. 1 and 50 characters are saved exactly. After refresh no blank or over-length category exists.

scenario: Duplicate category name in the same store
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-1 Bags exists.
steps: 1. Create a category with each name, one per attempt.
expected: All three are blocked with a message that the category already exists. Only one Bags category exists after refresh.

scenario: Same category name in a different store
pre: Logged in as Seller 2.
steps:
1. Create a category named Bags.
2. Log in as Seller 1 and check Seller 1's categories.
expected: Seller 2's Bags is created. Seller 1's categories are unchanged (store categories are unique per store only).

scenario: Rename a category to a duplicate name
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-1 Bags and CAT-5 Kitchen & Dining exist.
steps: 1. Rename Kitchen & Dining to 'bags'.
expected: Blocked with the duplicate-name message. CAT-5 keeps its old name.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Rename CAT-5 Kitchen & Dining to Kitchen.
2. Move Kitchen to the top of the list and save.
3. Refresh, then open the store page as Buyer 1.
expected: After refresh and on the store page, Kitchen is first and uses the new name. P-04 is still in it. No other category changed position except as moved.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-1 Bags contains P-01.
steps:
1. Hide CAT-1.
2. As Buyer 1, open the store page.
3. Open the old Bags category URL directly.
4. Search for 'Abaca Tote'.
expected: Bags is not shown on the store page and its direct URL shows 'not found' or redirects to the store page. P-01 is still found by search and its product page works (only the category is hidden).

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-1 is hidden.
steps:
1. Show CAT-1.
2. Open the store page as Buyer 1.
expected: Bags appears again in its previous position with P-01 in it.

scenario: Delete a category that still has products
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-4 Baskets contains P-02 only.
steps:
1. Click Delete on CAT-4.
2. Read the warning and click Cancel. Check that CAT-4 still exists.
3. Click Delete again and confirm.
4. Open P-02 in Product Management.
5. As Buyer 1, open P-02 and the store page.
expected: The warning states that 1 product will move to Uncategorized. Cancel leaves everything unchanged. After confirming, CAT-4 is gone, P-02's store category is Uncategorized, and P-02 is still Active and buyable. P-02 is never deleted or hidden.

scenario: Delete a parent category with subcategories
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-2 Home Decor has subcategories Lamps (P-03) and Baskets (P-02).
steps: 1. Delete CAT-2 and confirm.
expected: The warning lists both subcategories and the 2 products affected. After confirming, Home Decor, Lamps and Baskets are all gone, and P-02 and P-03 are in Uncategorized, still Active. No product is deleted.

scenario: Subcategory nesting at the depth limit
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). CAT-2 Home Decor > CAT-3 Lamps exists.
steps:
1. Create Wall Decor under Home Decor (level 2).
2. Try to create Table Lamps under Lamps (level 3).
data:
Level 2: Wall Decor (accept)
Level 3: Table Lamps (reject)
expected: Wall Decor is created at level 2. Lamps is not offered as a parent, or the save is blocked with a depth message. No level-3 category exists after refresh.

scenario: Product in several store categories at the limit
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Assign P-03 to Lamps, Best Sellers and Gift Ideas (3).
2. Try to add a 4th category, New Arrivals.
3. Open each category on the store page as Buyer 1.
expected: 3 categories are accepted and P-03 shows exactly once in each. The 4th is blocked with a limit message.

scenario: Store category is separate from platform category
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Edit P-01: change the store category to Kitchen & Dining; leave the platform category as Women's Bags.
2. As Buyer 1, browse the platform category Women's Bags.
3. Open Seller 1's store page, Kitchen & Dining.
expected: P-01 still appears under the platform category Women's Bags and now under the store's Kitchen & Dining. Changing the store category did not change the platform category, and sellers cannot create or rename platform categories.

scenario: Add and publish a product with all valid data
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Fill in every field with the test data and upload 2 images.
2. Click Publish.
3. Refresh the product list.
4. As Buyer 1, search for the name, open the platform category and the store page.
data:
Name: Buri Placemat Set
Description: Set of 6 placemats, handwoven buri palm.
Images: product_front.jpg, product_side.png
Platform category: Home & Living
Store category: Kitchen & Dining
Brand: No brand
Condition: New
Price: ₱299.00
Stock: 30
Weight: 0.6 kg
Size: 35 × 25 × 3 cm
expected: The product is saved as Active with exactly these values. Buyers find it in search, in Home & Living and in the store's Kitchen & Dining, showing ₱299.00 and 30 in stock. Images appear in the uploaded order.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Fill in all fields with valid data.
2. Clear one required field and click Publish.
3. Repeat for each field in the test data.
data: Clear in turn: Name, Description, Images, Platform category, Price, Stock, Weight
expected: Each attempt is blocked and a required-field message is shown on that field only. The other entered values (including uploaded images) are kept on the form. No product is created.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Enter each value, one per attempt, with all other fields valid.
2. Click Publish.
data:
Name 4 characters: Tote (reject)
Name 5: Totes (accept)
Name 120 (accept)
Name 121 (reject)
Description 19 characters (reject)
Description 20 (accept)
Description 3,000 (accept)
Description 3,001 (reject)
expected: Only the 'accept' values publish. Each 'reject' value shows a message with the exact limit.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Enter each price, one per attempt, with all other fields valid.
2. Click Publish.
expected: Only 1.00, 1.01, 999,999.99 and 1,000,000.00 are accepted and saved exactly. Every other value is rejected with a price message and nothing is created. 199.999 is never rounded silently to 200.00.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Enter each stock value, one per attempt.
2. Click Publish.
expected: Only whole numbers 0 to 99,999 are accepted. A product published with 0 stock shows Sold out to buyers.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Try to publish with 0 images.
2. Publish with 1 image.
3. Edit and add up to 9 images.
4. Try to add a 10th image.
expected: 0 images is blocked with a message. 1 and 9 images are saved. The 10th image cannot be added (the upload button is disabled or a limit message appears).

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps: 1. Upload each file as a product image, one at a time.
expected: Only the 5.0 MB JPG is accepted. The others are rejected with a message naming JPG/PNG and 5 MB, and are not added to the image list.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps: 1. Enter each value, one per attempt, and click Publish.
data:
Weight 0 (reject)
Weight -1 (reject)
Weight 0.01 kg (accept)
Dimensions 0 × 0 × 0 (reject)
Dimensions abc (reject)
expected: Zero, negative and non-numeric values are rejected with a message. 0.01 kg is saved and later charged as 1 kg at checkout.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Fill in the name only.
2. Click Save as Draft.
3. As Buyer 1, search for the name and open the product's URL directly.
expected: The draft is saved with status Draft and no validation errors for other fields. It never appears to buyers, and its URL shows 'not found' or 'unavailable'.

scenario: Publish a draft with missing data
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). The draft from the previous case exists.
steps: 1. Open the draft and click Publish without filling the other fields.
expected: Publishing is blocked with required-field messages. The product stays Draft.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 is Active. Buyer 1 has P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Deactivate P-02.
2. As Buyer 1, search for it, open its URL and open the cart.
3. Reactivate P-02 and repeat the checks.
expected: While inactive: P-02 is missing from search, category and store pages; its URL shows 'unavailable'; the cart line is marked unavailable and cannot be checked out. After reactivation everything returns with the same price, stock and images.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Click Duplicate on P-02.
2. Check the copy's fields and save it.
expected: The copy has the same details, a new product ID, and is saved as Draft. The original P-02 is unchanged and buyers see only one Rattan Fruit Basket.

scenario: Edit price of a product in a buyer's cart
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 has P-02 (₱450.00) in the cart.
steps:
1. Change P-02's price to ₱420.00 and save.
2. As Buyer 1, refresh the cart and go to checkout.
expected: The cart line and checkout both show ₱420.00 and the subtotal is recalculated. The old price is not used anywhere.

scenario: Delete a product with unfinished orders
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 is in an order with status To Ship.
steps: 1. Click Delete on P-02 and confirm.
expected: Deletion is blocked with a message that the product has unfinished orders. P-02 stays Active.

scenario: Delete a product with only finished orders
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-04 has only Completed orders.
steps:
1. Delete P-04 and confirm.
2. As Buyer 1, search for P-04 and open the completed order.
3. As Seller 1, open the same order.
expected: P-04 disappears from the product list, search and store page. Both order views still show its name, image and price paid.

scenario: Bulk deactivate and bulk delete with a mixed selection
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 has a To Ship order; P-04 and the Buri Placemat Set do not.
steps:
1. Select P-02, P-04 and Buri Placemat Set; choose Bulk Deactivate.
2. Reactivate all three, select them again and choose Bulk Delete.
expected: Bulk Deactivate deactivates all three. Bulk Delete deletes P-04 and Buri Placemat Set and reports that P-02 was skipped because it has unfinished orders. P-02 is still present.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Fill in valid data.
2. Double-click Publish quickly.
expected: Exactly one product is created.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Open the edit page of one of Seller 1's products.
2. Replace the product ID in the URL with P-05's ID (Seller 2) and load it.
3. Try to save.
expected: Access is denied (403 or not found). P-05's details are not shown and P-05 is unchanged.

scenario: Create a product with 2 variation types
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Add variation Color with options Red, Blue.
2. Add variation Size with options S, M, L.
3. Fill in price, stock and SKU for every row.
4. Publish.
5. As Buyer 1, open the product.
data:
Name: Buri Coin Purse
Color: Red, Blue
Size: S, M, L
Prices: S ₱99, M ₱129, L ₱149
Stock: 5 each
SKU: BCP-<COLOR>-<SIZE>
expected: Exactly 6 rows are generated (Red-S, Red-M, Red-L, Blue-S, Blue-M, Blue-L), each saved with its own price, stock and SKU. The buyer sees both selectors and the price range ₱99 – ₱149.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buri Coin Purse has Color and Size.
steps: 1. Try to add a third variation type.
expected: The third type cannot be added; a message states the maximum of 2. The existing 6 rows are unchanged.

scenario: Options per type at the limit
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Add 20 options to Color.
2. Try to add a 21st option.
expected: 20 options are accepted. The 21st is blocked with a limit message.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Under Color, add options Red and red.
2. Add an option with an empty name.
3. Click Publish.
expected: Publishing is blocked. The duplicate (not case-sensitive) and the empty option are each highlighted with a message. No product is created.

scenario: Missing or invalid price or stock on one variant
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Create Color × Size as above.
2. Leave Blue-L price blank and publish.
3. Enter Blue-L price ₱0.00 and publish.
4. Enter Blue-L stock -1 and publish.
expected: Each attempt is blocked and only the Blue-L row is highlighted. The price and stock rules from A17 apply per variant.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Add Product page is open.
steps:
1. Give Red-S and Blue-S the same SKU.
2. Then use an SKU already used by P-01.
3. Publish each time.
expected: Both are blocked with a duplicate-SKU message.

scenario: Price range shown on the product page and search
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-01 is published.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, search for 'Abaca Woven Tote Bag'.
2. Open P-01 without selecting a variant.
3. Select Natural-M.
expected: Search card and product page show ₱199 – ₱299. After selecting Natural-M the page shows ₱249.00 only.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Set image A for Natural and image B for Black.
2. As Buyer 1, select Natural, then Black.
expected: The main image changes to the selected colour's image each time.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-01 Black-M stock is 0.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, open P-01 and select Black.
2. Try to click M.
expected: M is visible but disabled for Black and cannot be selected. Natural-M remains selectable. The page shows no error.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A Completed order exists for P-01 Natural-M at ₱249.
steps:
1. Rename option Natural to Beige.
2. Change Beige-M price to ₱259.
3. Add option Brown.
4. Open the old order as Seller 1 and as Buyer 1.
expected: The old order still shows Natural-M at ₱249.00 for both roles. The product page shows Beige and Brown with the new price.

scenario: Remove a variant that is in a buyer's cart
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 has P-01 Black-L in the cart.
steps:
1. Delete the Black-L row and save.
2. As Buyer 1, open the cart and try to select and check out Black-L.
expected: The cart line shows 'Variation unavailable' and cannot be selected for checkout. Other cart lines still check out.

scenario: Remove a variant with unfinished orders
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-01 Natural-S is in a To Ship order.
steps:
1. Delete the Natural-S row and save.
2. Open the To Ship order.
expected: The delete is blocked with a message that the variant has unfinished orders. Natural-S stays on the product and the order can still be shipped.

scenario: Stock deducted when a COD order is placed
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 stock is 20.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, order 2 × P-02 by COD.
2. As Seller 1, refresh P-02's stock.
expected: Stock is exactly 18 immediately after the order is placed.

scenario: Stock deducted when an unpaid e-wallet order is placed
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 stock is 20.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, place an e-wallet order for 1 × P-02 but do not pay.
2. Check P-02's stock.
expected: Stock is 19 while the order is To Pay.

scenario: Stock restored when the buyer cancels
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A COD order for 2 × P-02 exists; stock is 18.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, cancel the order.
2. Check P-02's stock.
expected: Stock returns to exactly 20.

scenario: Stock restored on auto-cancel of an unpaid order
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). An unpaid e-wallet order for 1 × P-02 exists; stock is 19.
steps:
1. Wait 1 hour after the order was placed.
2. Check the order and P-02's stock.
expected: The order is Cancelled (unpaid) and stock is back to 20.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-01 Natural-M stock is 8, Natural-L is 5.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, order 1 × Natural-M.
2. Check every P-01 variant's stock.
expected: Natural-M is 7. Every other variant is unchanged.

scenario: Overselling: 1 left, 2 buyers check out at once
pre: P-03 stock is 1. Buyer 1 and Buyer 2 each have P-03 in the cart on separate devices, both on the checkout page.
steps:
1. Both buyers click Place Order at the same moment (count down together).
2. Check both buyers' orders and P-03's stock.
expected: Exactly one order is created. The other buyer gets an out-of-stock message and has no order and no charge. Stock is 0, never −1.

pre: P-07 (Seller 2) stock is set to 1.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, buy the last unit.
2. As Buyer 2, open P-07 and search for it.
3. As Seller 2, open the product list.
expected: Buyer 2 sees 'Sold out' with Add to Cart and Buy Now disabled. Seller 2's list shows Out of Stock.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 stock is 7.
steps:
1. Sell 1 unit (stock 6) and check alerts.
2. Sell 1 more (stock 5) and check alerts.
3. Sell 1 more (stock 4) and check alerts.
expected: No alert at 6. Exactly one alert at 5. No new alert at 4 (once per crossing).

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Set P-02 stock to each value, one per attempt, and save.
expected: Only 0 and 99,999 are saved. Each invalid value shows a message and the previous stock is kept.

scenario: Reduce stock below the quantity in a cart
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 has 5 × P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Set P-02 stock to 3.
2. As Buyer 1, open the cart and click Check Out.
expected: The cart shows 'Only 3 left' and blocks checkout until the quantity is 3 or fewer. No order for 5 units can be placed.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create a sale for P-02 at 20% off.
2. Set start 10 minutes from now and end 2 hours from now.
3. Save.
4. As Buyer 1, open P-02 before the start time.
expected: The sale is listed as Upcoming with the exact times. Before the start, buyers see ₱450.00 and no badge.

scenario: Sale goes live at the exact start time
pre: The sale above is Upcoming.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, open P-02 one minute before the start time.
2. Refresh one minute after the start time.
3. Add P-02 to the cart and open checkout.
expected: Before: ₱450.00. After: ₱360.00 with ₱450.00 struck through and a −20% badge. Cart and checkout also show ₱360.00.

scenario: Sale ends at the exact end time
pre: The sale is Ongoing. Buyer 1 has P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Open P-02 one minute before the end time.
2. Refresh one minute after the end time.
3. Refresh the cart and checkout.
expected: After the end time the price is ₱450.00 everywhere: product page, search card, cart and checkout. The badge and struck-through price are gone.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Try to save a sale with each date combination.
data:
End before start (reject)
Start = end (reject)
Start in the past (reject)
expected: Each is rejected with a date message. No sale is created.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Enter each discount for P-02, one per attempt, and save.
expected: Only whole percentages from 1% to 99% are accepted, and the preview shows the exact sale price.

scenario: Fixed sale price at or above the original
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Set a fixed sale price for P-02, one per attempt.
expected: Only prices from ₱1.00 up to below ₱450.00 are accepted.

scenario: Overlapping sales on the same product
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 has a sale today 13:00–15:00.
steps: 1. Create another sale for P-02 today 14:00–16:00.
expected: Rejected with a message that P-02 already has a sale in that period.

scenario: Sale on a product with variants
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Put P-01 on 10% off.
2. As Buyer 1, select each size of Natural.
expected: Prices show ₱179.10, ₱224.10 and ₱269.10, and the range is ₱179.10 – ₱269.10.

pre: A 20% sale on P-02 is Ongoing. Buyer 1 placed an order at ₱360.00 during it.
steps:
1. Change the discount to 30% and save.
2. As Buyer 2, open P-02.
3. Open Buyer 1's earlier order.
expected: Buyer 2 sees ₱315.00 immediately. Buyer 1's earlier order still shows ₱360.00.

pre: The sale is Ongoing.
steps:
1. Click End Now and confirm.
2. As Buyer 1, refresh P-02 and the cart.
expected: The sale shows Ended and buyers see ₱450.00 at once in every view.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create a voucher with the test data.
2. Save.
3. As Buyer 1, open Seller 1's store page and P-02.
data:
Code: MCH50
Type: Fixed ₱50 off
Min spend: ₱300
Total usage: 100
Per buyer: 1
Valid: this month
Applies to: all products
Display: claimable
expected: The voucher is saved as Ongoing. The store page and P-02's page show 'Claim ₱50 off, min. spend ₱300' with a Claim button.

scenario: Create a percentage voucher with a cap
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create MCH10 with the test data.
2. As Buyer 1, claim it and check out ₱600 of Seller 1 items, then ₱1,250 (P-03).
expected: The ₱600 checkout gets exactly ₱60.00 off. The ₱1,250 checkout gets exactly ₱100.00 off (not ₱125.00).

pre: Logged in as Seller 2.
steps:
1. Create RVSECRET as code-only.
2. As Buyer 1, check Seller 2's store page and product pages.
3. Check out ₱1,499 (P-06) and type 'rvsecret' in the voucher box.
expected: The voucher is not listed anywhere on the buyer side. Typing the code in lower case applies ₱100.00 off.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Try to save a voucher with each code, one per attempt.
data:
ABC (3, reject)
ABCD (4, accept)
ABCDEFGHIJKL (12, accept)
ABCDEFGHIJKLM (13, reject)
MCH 50 (space, reject)
MCH-50 (symbol, reject)
mch75 (accept, saved as MCH75)
expected: Only the 'accept' codes save, and they are saved in upper case.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). MCH50 exists. PLAT100 exists (platform).
steps: 1. Create a voucher with each code.
expected: All are rejected as duplicates.

scenario: Discount larger than the minimum spend
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create a ₱500-off voucher with a ₱100 minimum spend.
2. Create a ₱100-off voucher with a ₱100 minimum spend.
expected: The first is blocked with a message that the discount cannot exceed the minimum spend. The second (equal) is accepted.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Try to save a voucher with each invalid value.
data:
Amount ₱0 (reject)
Percentage 0% (reject)
Percentage 100% (reject)
Cap ₱0 on a % voucher (reject)
Total usage 0 (reject)
Per buyer 2 with total usage 1 (reject)
End before start (reject)
expected: Each is rejected with a message on the field. Nothing is saved.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create MCHTOTE: ₱30 off, min spend ₱100, P-01 only.
2. As Buyer 1, check out P-02 alone and try the voucher.
3. Check out P-01 Natural-M alone and apply it.
4. Check out P-01 + P-02 together and apply it.
expected: P-02 alone: not applicable. P-01 alone: ₱30 off. P-01 + P-02: ₱30 off, and minimum spend counts only the P-01 amount.

scenario: Edit a voucher buyers already claimed
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 has claimed MCH50.
steps:
1. Try to change the minimum spend to ₱500.
2. Try to change the amount to ₱20.
3. Extend the end date by 7 days.
4. Raise the total usage to 150.
expected: Minimum spend and amount are locked (cannot be edited). The new end date and usage limit save. Buyer 1's wallet shows the new end date.

scenario: End a voucher buyers already claimed
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 has claimed MCH50; Buyer 2 used MCH50 on a To Ship order.
steps:
1. End MCH50 and confirm.
2. Check Buyer 1's wallet and checkout.
3. Open Buyer 2's order.
expected: Buyer 1's wallet no longer offers MCH50 and checkout cannot apply it. Buyer 2's order still shows ₱50.00 off.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, use MCH50 on an order.
2. Check MCH50's usage.
3. As Buyer 1, cancel the order and check again.
expected: Usage shows 1 of 100 after the order and 0 of 100 after the cancellation.

scenario: Create a flash sale in a time slot
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Create a flash sale for P-02 in today's 12:00–14:00 slot, flash price ₱299, flash quantity 3.
2. Save.
3. As Buyer 1, open P-02 at 11:59 and at 12:00.
expected: Saved as Upcoming. At 11:59 buyers see ₱450 (with an 'upcoming flash sale' notice if supported). At 12:00 they see ₱299, a countdown to 14:00 and '3 left'.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 stock is 20.
steps: 1. Enter each value, one per attempt.
data:
Quantity 0 (reject)
Quantity 20 (accept)
Quantity 21 (reject)
Flash price ₱450 (reject)
Flash price ₱449.99 (accept)
expected: Only the 'accept' values save.

scenario: Price returns to normal when flash quantity runs out
pre: Flash sale live, 3 flash units left, no store sale.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, buy 3 × P-02.
2. As Buyer 2, refresh P-02 and add it to the cart.
expected: Buyer 1 pays ₱299 × 3 = ₱897. Buyer 2 sees ₱450 with no flash label, in both the product page and the cart.

scenario: Order more than the remaining flash quantity
pre: Flash sale live, 1 flash unit left, no store sale.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, add 2 × P-02 and open checkout.
2. Place the order.
expected: Checkout shows two lines: 1 × ₱299 and 1 × ₱450, total ₱749 before shipping. The order and the seller's view show the same split.

scenario: Flash sale ends at the slot end
pre: Flash sale live with units left. Buyer 1 has P-02 in the cart.
steps:
1. Watch P-02 at 14:00.
2. Refresh the cart and checkout.
expected: The countdown reaches 0 and the price returns to ₱450 in every view, with no error page.

scenario: Overlapping store sale and flash sale
pre: P-02 has a store sale at ₱360 and a flash sale at ₱299 at the same time, 1 flash unit left.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, open P-02.
2. Add 2 to the cart and open checkout.
expected: The product page shows ₱299. Checkout shows 1 × ₱299 and 1 × ₱360 (the store sale, not ₱450).

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Bundle: any 3 items from P-01 for 15% off.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, add 2 × P-01 Natural-S and check the cart.
2. Add 1 × P-01 Black-L and check again.
3. Remove one Natural-S.
expected: With 2 items: no discount. With 3 mixed variants: 15% of ₱697 = ₱104.55 off. After removing one: discount removed.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Promotion: buy 2 × P-02, get 1 × P-04 free (P-04 restocked to 10).
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, add 2 × P-02 and 1 × P-04.
2. Remove one P-02.
expected: With 2 × P-02, P-04 shows ₱0.00. With 1 × P-02, P-04 returns to ₱350.00.

scenario: Order list tabs, counts and filters
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). At least one order exists in each status.
steps:
1. Open each tab: New, To Ship, Shipping, Completed, Cancelled, Return/Refund.
2. Compare each tab's count with its rows.
3. Filter by a date range and search by an order ID.
expected: Each order appears in exactly one tab, matching its status; tab counts equal the rows. Date filter and search return exactly the matching orders.

scenario: Accept, pack, ready for pickup and print waybill
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A new COD order from Buyer 1 (P-02, ADDR-1) exists.
steps:
1. Click Accept.
2. Click Mark as Packed.
3. Click Ready for Pickup.
4. Print the waybill.
5. As Buyer 1 and Logistics 1, open the order or shipment.
expected: Status moves New → Accepted → Packed → Ready for Pickup, each with a timestamp. The waybill shows the tracking number, buyer's ADDR-1, Seller 1's pickup address, 0.8 kg and COD ₱500.00. Logistics 1 sees the parcel in the pickup queue. Buyer 1's timeline shows each step.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A new order exists.
steps:
1. Look for Ready for Pickup before accepting.
2. Try the Ready for Pickup request directly if possible.
expected: Only Accept (and Cancel) are available. A direct request is rejected and the status stays New.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A COD order (2 × P-02, MCH50) is Accepted. P-02 stock is 18.
steps:
1. Click Cancel.
2. Submit without a reason.
3. Choose 'Out of stock' and confirm.
expected: A reason is required. After cancelling: status Cancelled for both sides, P-02 stock 20, MCH50 back in Buyer 1's wallet, and Buyer 1 notified with the reason.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A paid e-wallet order is Accepted.
steps:
1. Cancel with the reason 'Out of stock'.
2. Check the order's refund status as Buyer 1.
expected: The order is Cancelled and a refund for the full amount paid is started. The amount is not counted in Seller 1's earnings.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Rider 1 has picked up the parcel.
steps:
1. Look for Cancel and Edit on the order.
2. Try the cancel request directly if possible.
expected: Cancel and Edit are not shown. A direct cancel request is rejected and the status is unchanged.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). The worked checkout example order exists.
steps: 1. Open Seller 1's order from the example.
expected: Shows Abaca Tote Natural-M × 1 at ₱249.00, Rattan Basket × 1 at ₱450.00, MCH50 −₱50.00, shipping ₱65.00, the buyer's note, payment method COD and ADDR-1. Seller 2's item is not in this order.

scenario: Seller cannot open another store's order
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Open one of Seller 1's orders.
2. Change the order ID in the URL to Seller 2's order from the worked example.
expected: Access is denied. No details of Seller 2's order are shown.

scenario: View a return request with evidence
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 requested a return for P-02 with 2 photos.
steps: 1. Open Return/Refund and the request.
expected: Shows the reason, description, both photos (full size on click), item, amount and the response deadline (3 days).

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A pending return request exists.
steps:
1. Click Approve.
2. As Buyer 1, open the order.
expected: Status Return Approved on both sides. Buyer 1 is notified and sees return instructions. The amount moves out of Seller 1's pending earnings.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A pending return request exists.
steps: 1. Click Reject and submit with an empty reason, then with 9 characters.
expected: Both are blocked; the reason needs 10–300 characters. The request stays pending.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Reject with the test reason.
2. As Buyer 1, open the request.
data: Reason: Item shows signs of use and the tag is removed.
expected: Status Rejected on both sides; Buyer 1 sees the exact reason and an Escalate button.

pre: The request was rejected less than 3 days ago.
steps:
1. As Buyer 1, click Escalate.
2. As Seller 1, open the request.
3. As Buyer 1, try to escalate again.
expected: Status In Dispute for both sides. Seller 1 can no longer approve or reject. A second escalation is not possible.

pre: A return request was submitted.
steps: 1. Do not respond. Check the request just before and just after 3 days.
expected: Pending before 3 days; Auto-approved after, and Buyer 1 is notified.

pre: A return for P-02 (₱450.00) was approved and refunded.
steps: 1. Open Sales Reports and Earnings.
expected: ₱450.00 and its commission are excluded from gross sales and earnings.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). P-02 has a 5-star, a 3-star and a 1-star review.
steps:
1. Open Reviews.
2. Filter by 1 star, then 5 stars.
expected: All 3 reviews are listed with stars, text, photos, variant and date. Each filter shows only matching reviews.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Reply to the 5-star review.
2. As Buyer 1, open P-02's reviews.
data: Reply: Salamat po! Enjoy your basket.
expected: The reply appears under that review, labelled as the seller's response.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A reply exists.
steps:
1. Try to post a second reply to the same review.
2. Edit the first reply.
expected: A second reply is not possible. The edit saves and replaces the first reply.

scenario: Seller cannot delete or hide a review
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Look for Delete or Hide on the 1-star review.
2. Try a delete request directly if possible.
expected: No Delete or Hide option. A direct request is rejected (403). The review is still visible to buyers.

scenario: Chat with a buyer, with attachment
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Buyer 1 sent a message about P-02.
steps:
1. Reply with text and attach review_photo.jpg.
2. As Buyer 1, open the chat.
expected: Buyer 1 receives the text and the image in the right order with timestamps.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Attach each file.
expected: All three are rejected with a message and nothing is sent.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Send an empty message.
2. Send a message of spaces only.
3. Send 1,000 characters.
4. Send 1,001 characters.
expected: Empty and spaces-only messages are not sent. 1,000 characters are sent in full. 1,001 are blocked or input stops at 1,000.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). The worked checkout example order is Completed.
steps: 1. Open Earnings and the order's breakdown.
expected: Gross ₱699.00; seller voucher −₱50.00; commission −₱32.45; net ₱616.55. PLAT100 (₱63.66 share), FREESHIP and the ₱65.00 shipping fee do not appear as deductions.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). The example order is Delivered, not Completed.
steps:
1. Check Pending and Available balances.
2. As Buyer 1, click Order Received.
3. Check the balances again.
expected: Before: ₱616.55 in Pending, not in Available. After: ₱616.55 moved to Available; Pending reduced by the same amount.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). One cancelled and one refunded order exist in the period.
steps: 1. Open Sales Reports for the period.
expected: Neither order adds to gross sales, commission or earnings. They are not counted in the completed-order count.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps:
1. Filter today, last 7 days, and a custom range that starts and ends on an order's date.
2. Try an end date before the start date.
expected: Totals match the orders in each range, and an order on the start or end date is included. The invalid range is rejected.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). Available balance ₱616.55; no pending payout.
steps: 1. Request each amount, one per attempt (cancel any successful request before the next one).
expected: Only ₱100.00 and ₱616.55 are accepted. A valid request lowers Available by that amount and shows a Pending payout.

scenario: Second payout while one is pending
pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved). A ₱100.00 payout is pending.
steps: 1. Request another ₱100.00.
expected: Blocked with a message that a payout is already pending.

pre: Logged in as Seller 1 (Approved).
steps: 1. Double-click Request Payout.
expected: Exactly one payout request exists and Available is lowered once.
